about: Raiders of the time (Plans/ai_fleets.md, phase 4): who went out, from where, when, how many, what they struck and where they sold what they took. Bands of longships go out in the sailing season, raid a place they can overwhelm (or take a trader at sea they can catch), sell the loot and captives at a Norse market and go home. The dated raids of the chronicle (chronicle_793.json) hit the markets on their days as well; these bands are the rest of the sea's danger. Numbers are starting guesses from the sources noted; uncertain items are marked (?).
units: days of the year (1-365); men; real km; knots; deniers

season.about: out about 1 May, home by 30 September (?)

pressure.about: bands out a season, by year (the last year listed holds after it); pressure_x scales it (1 = history; tests and harness can turn it up)

origins.name: Northmen of the west of Norway
origins.basis: ASC 789 (three ships 'of Hordaland' at Portland), 793 Lindisfarne, 794 Jarrow, 795 Iona, Rathlin and Skye, 798 Inis Patraic, 799 the islands off Aquitaine (?): the first raiders came from western Norway (Hordaland, Rogaland) by the northern isles

origins.name: Danes
origins.basis: RFA 800 (Charles fortifies the coast against pirates infesting the Gallic sea), 810 (Godfred's fleet of 200 ships on the Frisian islands, tribute of 100 pounds): Danish raiding of Frisia and Flanders from c. 800 (?)

band.about: a band of 1-3 longships of about 30 men each (?)

defence.about: fighting men a place can put up at short notice, by its kind (times 1 + 0.25 x (size - 2)) (?)

raid.about: a raided market keeps 35% of its stock, 45% dearer, fading over the weeks (trade_rules: shock_fade); the band takes half of what's left worth carrying; captives where people are easily taken; a place isn't raided again for 60 days

at_sea.about: raiders look for prey within sight; they row a sprint, then a steady pull, and give up after 8 game hours; a taken ship loses 60% of her cargo (their room allowing) and half her silver

player.about: tribute to be let go; parley in a shared tongue (the merchant speaks Frisian and some Norse (?)); submitting gives up the cargo and most of the silver; losing a fight costs men too; the chase's status every 15 game minutes
